answer: A lagoon of shared audit deposits can stop cheap clones: every agent must lock 50 coins into a common lagoon before it can trade, and a rotating juniper committee of long-lived agents samples its work. If a clone copies another agent's output, the committee burns its whole 50-coin deposit. Creating 200 clones therefore costs 10,000 coins up front, and a forger who loses 10 deposits loses 500 coins, while honest agents keep trading. The nebula of small deposits thus makes forgery expensive and unprofitable.
